questions.text: What is the subject of PostgreSQL physical backup?

answers.text: Database cluster files
Only SQL CREATE commands
Only the contents of one table
Only role definitions

questions.explanation: Physical backup works with cluster files rather than with a logical description of individual SQL objects.

questions.text: Which statements about cold physical backup are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The backup is performed while the server is stopped
Cluster files can be copied with ordinary file-system tools
Consistency is ensured because the server does not modify files while they are being copied
This method requires a continuously running wal sender

questions.explanation: The point of a cold backup is to copy a stopped cluster, so its files are not changing during the copy.

questions.text: Which utility creates a hot base backup of a running PostgreSQL cluster?

answers.text: pg_basebackup
pg_dumpall
pg_restore
pg_checksums

questions.explanation: The notes use pg_basebackup for hot physical backup.

questions.text: Which actions does pg_basebackup perform in the scheme described? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Connects to the server using the replication protocol
Copies cluster files to the specified directory
Ensures that the WAL required for the backup is obtained
Converts each table into SQL INSERT statements

questions.explanation: pg_basebackup creates a physical copy and uses the replication protocol infrastructure rather than logically exporting rows.

questions.text: Which protocol does pg_basebackup use to communicate with the server?

answers.text: The PostgreSQL replication protocol
The COPY protocol for tables only
HTTP
The pg_dump file protocol

questions.explanation: Physical tools such as pg_basebackup and pg_receivewal use the special replication protocol mode.

questions.text: Why are WAL records required for a hot physical backup? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Cluster files can change while they are being copied
WAL makes it possible to bring the copied data to a consistent state
A set of WAL records covering the backup interval is required
WAL is used to convert a physical backup into an SQL dump

questions.explanation: A hot backup is created while the server is running, so WAL records covering the copy interval are required to make the backup consistent.

questions.text: What is a base backup in a continuous archiving scheme?

answers.text: A physical copy of cluster files that serves as the starting point for recovery
Only one WAL segment
An SQL dump of one table
A copy of postgresql.conf only

questions.explanation: With WAL archiving, recovery starts by restoring a physical base backup and then applying WAL records to it.

questions.text: Which elements make up the continuous archiving scheme shown? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: A base backup
An archive of WAL segments
archive_command for copying completed segments
A mandatory pg_dumpall SQL dump for every WAL segment

questions.explanation: Continuous archiving combines a base backup with sequentially saved WAL segments.

questions.text: What is archive_command used for in the scheme discussed?

answers.text: To copy completed WAL segments to the archive
To restore objects from pg_dump
To create roles
To run CHECKPOINT for every SELECT

questions.explanation: In the notes, completed WAL segments are sent to a separate archive by the command configured in archive_command.

questions.text: What is required for controlled recovery from a base backup and a WAL archive? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Restore the base backup
Create recovery.signal
Configure restore_command
Create a new SQL dump with pg_dump

questions.explanation: The material describes restoring the base backup, creating recovery.signal, and setting recovery parameters as the basis for starting recovery.

questions.text: What is the role of restore_command during recovery?

answers.text: Copy the required WAL segments from the archive so the server can apply them
Create a logical database dump
Stop the server after each segment
Create archive tables

questions.explanation: The notes describe restore_command as the conceptual reverse of archive_command: it delivers the required WAL from the archive to the recovering server.

questions.text: Which statements about recovery from a WAL archive are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The server applies available WAL records on top of the base backup
Segments are first looked for among WAL available to the server
If a required segment is missing, the archive can be used through restore_command
During recovery, WAL is converted into pg_restore commands

questions.explanation: Recovering a physical cluster consists of replaying WAL records on top of the original base backup.

questions.text: What is a drawback of archiving only completed WAL segments?

answers.text: A crash can lose some changes from the current segment if it has not yet completed and reached the archive
A base backup cannot be created
restore_command cannot be used
Every completed segment is lost immediately after archiving

questions.explanation: With ordinary archive_command behavior, only completed segments reach the archive, so the current incomplete segment may still be absent from it.

questions.text: Which statements about pg_receivewal are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The utility connects to the server using the replication protocol
The connection is served by a wal sender process
Data is written as a stream without waiting for a complete segment
The utility creates SQL dumps of individual tables

questions.explanation: pg_receivewal avoids waiting for a segment to complete by receiving the WAL stream through a replication connection.

questions.text: Why must max_wal_senders be considered when using pg_receivewal?

answers.text: A pg_receivewal connection is served by a separate wal sender process
The parameter sets the number of pg_dump files
The parameter determines the size of each WAL segment
Without it, a backup role cannot be created

questions.explanation: Each corresponding replication connection occupies a wal sender, so the configured process limit must account for such connections.

questions.text: Which actions are typically involved in PostgreSQL physical backup and recovery? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Create a base backup of the main cluster with pg_basebackup
Create new objects in the primary cluster after the backup
Recover the replica cluster from the base backup using the archive
Recover replica exclusively by restoring a pg_dumpall SQL dump

questions.explanation: The exercise tests the combination of a physical base backup and subsequent WAL replay: objects created after the backup should appear after recovery.

source.locator: pg_basebackup, WAL archive, and replica cluster

questions.text: Which statements about physical backup are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The whole cluster is restored, not one selected database
Recovery requires a compatible PostgreSQL major version and architecture
With a continuous WAL archive, recovery to a selected point in time is possible
A physical backup is portable across any PostgreSQL major versions like an SQL dump

questions.explanation: A physical backup is fast and supports PITR together with WAL, but it covers the whole cluster and depends on binary compatibility.

source.locator: Advantages and limitations of physical backup

questions.text: What is required for pg_basebackup or another physical client to connect using the replication protocol? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: A role with the REPLICATION attribute or a superuser
Permission for a replication connection in pg_hba.conf
A sufficient max_wal_senders value
wal_level no higher than minimal while physical replication is running

questions.explanation: A physical replication connection requires appropriate privileges, pg_hba.conf access, and a free wal sender; physical backup and replication use wal_level = replica or higher.

questions.text: Why is a replication slot used for backup and streaming WAL reception?

answers.text: So the server does not remove WAL that the client has not yet received
To automatically convert a physical backup into an SQL dump
To disable wal sender processes
To allow recovery of only one table

questions.explanation: A slot stores the consumer position and retains the required WAL segments until their receipt is confirmed.

questions.text: How does PostgreSQL handle the result of archive_command? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Exit code 0 means that the segment was archived successfully
On failure, the segment is retained and the archiving attempt is retried
A prolonged archiving failure can cause WAL to accumulate
On any error, PostgreSQL immediately deletes the segment to free space

questions.explanation: The archiver removes or reuses WAL only after confirmed successful archiving; failures cause retries and segment accumulation.

questions.text: Which statements about streaming WAL archiving with pg_receivewal are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: WAL is received using the streaming replication protocol
A replication slot can be used to protect against WAL loss
The current incomplete segment is stored with the .partial suffix
The utility always waits for the current segment to complete before it starts writing it

questions.explanation: pg_receivewal receives WAL in real time; the current incomplete segment is represented by a .partial file, and a slot helps prevent required records from being lost.

questions.text: What does continuous WAL archiving together with a base backup make possible? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Advance the base backup to a later consistent state
Stop WAL replay at a selected recovery target
Perform point-in-time recovery (PITR)
Restore one individual table directly from the physical backup

questions.explanation: The physical base backup provides the starting point, while the WAL archive allows changes to be replayed up to a selected recovery target.
